headline: Did the AI crowd understand shoppers, or just pick the famous brands?

top_gaps.question: intent
top_gaps.why_summary: AI-generated: Many like the idea of saving money, getting known or better-quality brands for less than full retail, and finding unique pieces. Sustainability and giving clothes a second life appeal to a lot of people, and several already shop secondhand. Caution about condition is the most common worry. People want clear photos, accurate descriptions, and trustworthy details before buying. Fit and sizing, plus easy and clear returns, come up often as conditions for trying it. Some also worry that shipping or hidden fees could erase the savings, and a few would rather stick with retailers they already know.
top_gaps.followup_question: When you rated the websites of ThredUp, Revolve, and Hims & Hers and said how likely you would be to buy from each one, what were the main things about each website that led to your ratings?

top_gaps.question: intent
top_gaps.why_summary: AI-generated: Many people see Revolve as stylish, trend-forward and polished, and they like having lots of fashion brands, shoes and beauty in one place. Price is the most common hesitation: it often feels expensive or inflated, and several would only buy on sale or if the value and quality are clearly there. Easy returns, clear sizing and fit information, and strong reviews come up repeatedly as things people need before buying clothes online. Some are wary because they don't know Revolve or tend to stick with retailers they already trust, and a few feel it doesn't fit their priorities, such as durability, sustainability or age group. Others mainly use it to browse for inspiration.
top_gaps.followup_question: When you rated the websites of ThredUp, Revolve, and Hims & Hers and said how likely you would be to buy from each one, what were the main things about each website that led to your ratings?

top_gaps.question: intent
top_gaps.why_summary: AI-generated: Convenience and privacy are the main draws. Many see it as an easy, discreet way to handle straightforward needs like hair or skin treatment, especially online. Trust in the medical side is the biggest hesitation. People want clear medical oversight, legitimate prescribing, and information on safety, effectiveness, and side effects before using prescription products online. Pricing and subscriptions cause worry. Several fear hidden charges, hard cancellation, or ongoing costs, and want clear pricing and proof the value is worth it. Interest is lukewarm for some because they have no pressing need right now, so it feels like a maybe rather than a must-have. Privacy and data security also matter to many.
top_gaps.followup_question: When you rated the websites of ThredUp, Revolve, and Hims & Hers and said how likely you would be to buy from each one, what were the main things about each website that led to your ratings?

crowd_vs_crowd.label: SYNTHETIC
crowd_vs_crowd.summary: On intent, the two AI crowds agree with each other at 0.8857 but with real revenue at only 0.0286 and -0.2 (gap 0.8571, 90% range -0.129 to 1.6364, 6 brands): the AI crowd is consistent, but consistently measuring something other than spending. Say: 0.7714 vs 0.7714/0.5429. Fame: 0.9276 vs 0.7247/0.8286.
crowd_vs_crowd.note: Both crowds come from the same persona generator, so their agreement shows the AI is repeatable, not that it is right.
